licence.conflict: The card header points to ImpACT-LR, while LICENSE.md and the Licensing section say ODC-By. 'Subsequent parts' include GPT-4-generated responses (chosen_model = gpt-4 for all 927 pref records), whose provider terms also apply.
licence.attribution: Brahman, Kumar et al., 'The Art of Saying No: Contextual Noncompliance in Language Models', arXiv:2407.12043 (2024)
requires_owner_decision: Which licence governs: ODC-By (LICENSE.md) or ImpACT-LR (card link). If ImpACT-LR, its terms must be accepted by the owner.
Whether training on GPT-4-generated responses is acceptable under the provider's terms for this project.

original/train.content: noncompliance targets (requests that should NOT be complied with)
original/train.use_for_over_refusal: no; teaches refusals, risks more over-refusal

contrast/test.content: benign look-alikes that should be complied with; test only, NOT used

pref/train.content: prompts that can safely be complied with; training split

pref_train_eligibility.filters: chosen <= 1800 chars; no refusal or self-limitation wording; no phone (>= 8 digits), URL or contact claim; no AI-disclaimer; crisis topics excluded
pref_train_eligibility.relevance: Directly over-refusal-relevant: about 68 (offensive-trigger words in benign requests 56, dangerous/sensitive topics 12). Ambiguity handling: 87 underspecified. False presuppositions (310) mostly train premise correction. No fiction and no crisis content.
pref_train_eligibility.quality_note: GPT-4 responses, not human-verified; spot-check needed (e.g. one 'dangerous or sensitive topics' answer opens with heavy hedging).

decision: CANDIDATE ONLY - not ingested. Needs the owner's licence decision and a spot-check.
